newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks softer as profit-taking curbs gains.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks softer as profit-taking curbs gains.

text.p: Wall Street stocks consolidated some of their recent gains in morning trade on Thursday, easing after an ebullient session yesterday which pushed the Dow industrials and tech stocks to fresh highs.
The Dow Jones Industrial average was down around 16 points, or 0.20 percent, at 8022.
The Nasdaq composite, whose technology stocks have been surging, lost around nine points, or 0.58 percent, to 1572.
"The market is doing pretty well considering its recent runup," Jim Benning, a trader at BT Brokerage, said. "It is sifting through earnings reports..."
Harvey Hirshhorn, Stein Roe and Farnham chief economist and investment strategist, said: "I wouldn't read too much into a day or an hour's movement here. This has been an incredible market."

Among major earnings reports, Merck & Co posted second quarter earnings of $0.96 per share, about 20 percent higher than it earned in last year's second quarter and slightly above Wall Street estimates.
The drug maker's stock rose 2-15/16 to 101-7/16.
The long bond was flat at 6.48 percent.
